detail.message: My partner and I just got engaged and we are hosting a dinner for 30 in early December. I want something showstopping but I have no idea what. Inspire me?

ideas.title: Winter Citrus Wheel
ideas.description: A smooth white buttercream cake dressed with blood orange, lemon and lime wheels, with a few chamomile blooms and rosemary sprigs for a festive winter garden feel. A blood-orange tart alongside would make a lovely dessert-table moment.

ideas.title: Holiday Bramble & Pomegranate
ideas.description: A tall vanilla cake crowned with sugared cranberries, pomegranate and rosemary, adapted from Annie’s berry-and-chamomile cake for a jewel-toned winter centerpiece.

ideas.title: Peony & Chamomile Choux Crown
ideas.description: A celebration cake topped with caramel-glazed cream puffs and spun sugar, styled with pale blooms for an especially dramatic engagement-dinner centerpiece.

detail.reply: Congratulations to you both! For a December engagement dinner, I’d picture a winter citrus cake with blood orange, lemon and lime, little chamomile blooms and rosemary, with a blood-orange tart alongside. Or, for extra drama, a choux-crown centerpiece with caramel-glazed cream puffs and pale flowers. Which feels more like your evening—and are there any flavors or ingredients you especially love or need to avoid?

detail.message: It's my best friend's bridal shower in May, about 25 guests. Something romantic and a little vintage, maybe with a dessert table. Can you inspire me?

ideas.title: Blush Cherry Lambeth
ideas.description: An 8-inch vanilla cake for a romantic vintage feel, with soft blush buttercream, graceful piped borders and fresh raspberries. Annie’s Cherry Lambeth photo is the inspiration; for May, we can adapt it with seasonal spring berries and a raspberry tart alongside for the dessert table.

ideas.title: Sweetheart Spring Table
ideas.description: Ruffled white buttercream with strawberry hearts and raspberry filling, inspired by Annie’s Sweetheart cake. Add heart macarons and a raspberry tart for a candlelit bridal-shower dessert table.

ideas.title: Chamomile Choux Crown
ideas.description: A romantic centerpiece inspired by Annie’s Chamomile Choux Crown photo, with berry-and-cream layers, a caramel choux crown and delicate spring flowers. Pair it with seasonal tarts for a generous dessert table.

detail.reply:
For a romantic, slightly vintage feel, I’d look at Annie’s Cherry Lambeth cake: vanilla layers, soft blush buttercream, classic piped borders and spring berries, with a seasonal tart alongside. Another lovely option is the ruffled Sweetheart cake with strawberry hearts, heart macarons and a raspberry tart. For a more dramatic centerpiece, the Chamomile Choux Crown pairs beautifully with spring flowers and a tart for the dessert table.

Do you have a date in May in mind, and are there any flavors or allergies I should note?
